clue.text: Temple where father is filled with a divine spirit

indicators.note: the word for father has something placed inside it, so it is filled with the next pieces

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father
a god is a divine spirit

explanation.surface: A father is overcome with religious fervour in a place of worship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is filled with' puts A GOD inside PA, between its P and its A.
explanation.definitionFit: A pagoda is a tiered tower serving as a Buddhist or Hindu shrine in East Asia.

explanation.surface: Show where you are standing in a meadow.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, the fielding positions have names, and this is one of them, close to the batsman on the off side.
explanation.definitionFit: To indicate is to gesture at something with a finger; in cricket the fielder square of the batsman on the off side stands at this named spot.

parts.note: read not as a bloom like edelweiss but as something that flows slowly down Alpine valleys: a river of ice

explanation.surface: A bloom found high in the Alps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' looks like a plant but means a thing that flows.
explanation.definitionFit: A mass of ice creeping slowly downhill flows, so it is a flower in the cryptic sense.

clue.text: If you want to speak French, it's essential

definitions.text: If you want to speak French, it's essential

parts.words: If you want to speak French, it's essential
parts.note: the clue asks for the French way of saying something is essential, a phrase borrowed into English

explanation.surface: Advice that a learner of French cannot do without something.
explanation.walkthrough: The French phrase means required by etiquette or custom, and English uses it too.
explanation.definitionFit: The borrowed French phrase means obligatory, demanded by fashion or custom.

parts.note: a bar is a pub, here with its possessive s
AC is an abbreviation for account, a bill

explanation.surface: The tab at the local for a bottle of wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Barsac is a sweet white wine from the Bordeaux region of France.

clue.text: Separate audition is held for a role

definitions.text: audition is held for a role

explanation.surface: An actor is kept apart while trying out for a part.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits as two words, the article and a role in a play.
explanation.definitionFit: Separate means divided off from others; an audition is held to cast someone in one role, a single acting part.

indicators.note: one word sits inside the other, the skill placed in the bridge

parts.note: a span is the arch or length of a bridge, and to span is to bridge
art means skill, as in the art of cooking

explanation.surface: A clever old technique for the card game bridge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bridge' suggests the card game but gives SPAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A Spartan was a citizen of Sparta, the city-state of classical Greece.

clue.text: Two ways to operate? Get away!

explanation.surface: A surgeon is told the methods of working, then told to leave.
explanation.walkthrough: The first reading takes the three words separately: two methods of operating joined by 'and'.
explanation.definitionFit: Surgeons operate with a knife and machines operate when switched on, giving two methods; the idiom means flee in a hurry.

indicators.note: the letters of the next word are sorted into a new order

explanation.surface: A strange kind of coal-burning stove.
explanation.definitionFit: Odd and weird are synonyms for something strange.

clue.text: Is a good man able to get a game?

parts.note: to be able is can, read as a question opening 'Can...'
ST, saint, is a crossword stock for a good man

explanation.surface: A question whether a decent fellow is fit to play a game.
explanation.walkthrough: The question 'Is a good man able' turns into 'Can a saint', giving CAN A ST; then A from 'to get a'.
explanation.definitionFit: Canasta is a rummy-style card game played with two packs.

parts.note: the bench is the collective term for judges or magistrates
to mark is to notice or observe

explanation.surface: A standard by which judges should watch a case.
explanation.definitionFit: A benchmark is a standard or point of reference against which things are measured.

clue.text: Garment not worn out but full of holes

definitions.text: Garment not worn out but full of holes

parts.words: Garment not worn out but full of holes
parts.note: a new piece of clothing that is made of open mesh, so it has holes without being threadbare

explanation.surface: An item of clothing riddled with holes though not shabby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not worn out' sounds like threadbare, yet the holes are designed in: a mesh undershirt.
explanation.definitionFit: This mesh undershirt is knitted with large open holes by design.

indicators.note: the letters wanted lie inside the word attendance

explanation.surface: A nurse is present on the ward.
explanation.definitionFit: To nurse someone is to look after or care for them.

indicators.note: around: the word for feeling concern goes about the number

parts.note: to care is to feel concern
V is five in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Someone worried about a reduction in a figure.
explanation.definitionFit: To carve is to slice or cut, as meat at the table.

parts.note: not a café but a bar you snack on, a confectionery slab

explanation.surface: A place to buy a quick bite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Snack bar' suggests a café; the question mark says read it as a bar for snacking.
explanation.definitionFit: A bar of this sweet cocoa confection is a common snack.

clue.text: Possibly carry on taking oxygen in heart attack

indicators.note: the rearranged letters take in, or hold, the extra piece
possibly means the letters of carry on could be arranged otherwise

parts.note: O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: Advice to keep going on oxygen after someone has had a heart attack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' rearranges CARRY ON, and 'taking' puts O inside the result.
explanation.definitionFit: A coronary is short for coronary thrombosis, a blockage in an artery to the heart muscle.

parts.note: the legendary English bandit of Sherwood Forest, hunted by the Sheriff of Nottingham

explanation.surface: A fugitive on the run from the local lawman.
explanation.walkthrough: This legendary outlaw of Sherwood Forest robbed the rich to give to the poor; the Sheriff of Nottingham was his enemy.
explanation.definitionFit: The folk-hero bandit of English ballads was forever hunted by the Sheriff of Nottingham.

clue.text: How, initially, ownership may be established

definitions.text: How, initially, ownership may be established

parts.words: How, initially, ownership may be established
parts.note: the owner's initials, stitched or engraved on a possession, mark it as theirs

explanation.surface: A question of how one first proves something belongs to them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' looks like 'at first' but means by initials.
explanation.definitionFit: A design of interwoven initials put on linen or luggage identifies its owner.

indicators.note: motion means the letters of propose are set moving into a new order

explanation.surface: A debater's call to put a motion forward for someone on the other side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'motion' looks like a debating proposal but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who opposes, or argues against, a proposal.

explanation.surface: A society that neglects to make an announcement.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a captain may 'declare' to end the innings early; to carry on batting instead is to bat on.
explanation.definitionFit: A baton is a short stick or truncheon used as a club; in cricket a side that keeps batting rather than closing its innings has failed to declare.

parts.note: read not as a thing that goes down itself but as a weapon that, travelling underwater, sends ships to the bottom

explanation.surface: A thing that disappears below the sea surface.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sinks' looks intransitive but is transitive: this underwater missile sinks ships.
explanation.definitionFit: A self-propelled underwater missile travels beneath the surface to destroy ships.

parts.note: a public convenience is a toilet, a loo in British slang
P is the abbreviation for a penny

explanation.surface: A London Underground toilet charging a penny to enter.
explanation.walkthrough: The Circle line is a London Underground route; once public toilets cost a penny, hence 'spend a penny'.
explanation.definitionFit: A loop line is a railway route that runs round in a circle and rejoins itself.

parts.note: the vault of a bank, a secure chamber where valuables are kept

explanation.surface: A secure spot found on a river bank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Safe place' reads as a secure spot, but it is also the place where the safe is.
explanation.definitionFit: A vault or secure chamber in a bank stores money and valuables.

explanation.surface: A wheel's rod addressed the audience.
explanation.definitionFit: Made speech means talked or uttered words; a rod bracing the rim of a wheel against the hub is a supporting member.

clue.text: Not rounds used in an erratic salvo

indicators.note: erratic means the letters of salvo are scattered into a different order

explanation.surface: Not every round in a wild burst of gunfire is used.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rounds' suggests shots in the salvo; here it means circles.
explanation.definitionFit: Egg-shaped figures are elongated rather than perfect circles.

clue.text: Graduates meeting shortly? It's in the wind

parts.note: BAs are Bachelors of Arts, graduates
soon means shortly

explanation.surface: University graduates are soon to meet; rumour has it the news is in the air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the wind' suggests rumour; it means in the woodwind section.
explanation.definitionFit: This deep-toned double-reed instrument belongs to the woodwind section of an orchestra.

clue.text: Anticipated war breaking out with foes

indicators.note: breaking out means the letters of war and foes are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Conflict with enemies was predicted.
explanation.definitionFit: To have foreseen something is to have anticipated or predicted it.

clue.text: A good job student doesn't start

indicators.note: the word loses its opening letter

parts.note: a learner is a student

explanation.surface: A trainee fails to begin a well-paid position.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doesn't start' drops L from LEARNER.
explanation.definitionFit: A nice little earner, British idiom, is a profitable job.

clue.text: Contemptible cheat going back on promises to pay

indicators.note: the word for cheat is read backwards, going back

parts.note: to do someone is to cheat them
IOUs are written promises to pay a debt

explanation.surface: A swindler reneging on his debts is despicable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going back' turns DO into OD.
explanation.definitionFit: Odious means hateful, deserving of contempt.
